title: herbctl
description: The herbstluftwm keybind imperatives: every composite mod- binding as a plain-named verb - the float-register state machines, the navigation chains, the layout cyclers - compiled to a standalone bunli binary.

content.heading: herbctl - the keybind imperatives, as a native binary
content: herbctl owns what the keybinds used to express as inline herbstluftwm chains: one verb per mod-binding, each issuing the exact hlwm chains the binding expresses, token for token - compiled to a standalone binary with bunli, so the keybinds spawn binaries, not scripts. The verbs are named by what they do: split-right-cycle, shift-up, minimize-toggle - no whimsy (the original whimsical names were retired 2026-10; only the historical get-south/get-forward/get-deck/get-dedeck quartet keeps its name).
[https://github.com/akinevz2/herbctl](https://github.com/akinevz2/herbctl)

content.heading: The verbs
content: 25 verbs, one per keybind. Each verb gets its own section below.

content.heading: get-south
content: [$Mod-s] The zoom/peek grid, under lock: urgent jumpto when the tag has urgent windows, frame-down focus, the floating-layer branch (focusing the float layer AND failing through when it is empty), the cycle fallbacks, and a pseudotile toggle. One chained spawn, held under the hlwm lock.

content.heading: get-forward
content: [$Mod-w] Leave the floating layer, then cycle window/frame upward: focus --level=frame up, then cycle_frame. Under lock.

content.heading: get-deck
content: [$Mod-d] The layout cycler, count-gated: with 4+ windows in the focused frame it cycles max/vertical/grid/horizontal; with exactly 2 it cycles max/horizontal; otherwise a bare -1 rotation fallback.

content.heading: get-dedeck
content: [$ModShift-d] The shift-complement of get-deck: with >1 window in the focused frame it mixes in the max/grid/vertical layouts, otherwise it removes the focused frame.

content.heading: explode-frame
content: [$Mod-e] With >1 frame, cycle frames backward; otherwise explode the frame and cycle forward. The last split is never a dead end.

content.heading: focus-frame-left
content: [$Mod-a] Focus the frame to the left, or split one off at a third of the width when there is nothing to focus.

content.heading: focus-frame-down
content: [$Mod-b] Focus the frame down, else split a bottom frame at half and cycle into it.

content.heading: shift-up
content: [$ModShift-w] The shift-up ladder: first shift the window up into the frame above (--level=all); when there is nothing above, with >1 window in the focused frame cycle -1, otherwise try cycle_frame, then fall through to rotating the frame tree.

content.heading: rotate-tree
content: [$ModCtrl-r] Rotate the tree (<3 frames) or cycle frames forward; on a single frame it cycles windows in the opposite direction of the shift-up fallback.

content.heading: shift-down
content: [$ModShift-s] An empty focused frame is removed; a multi-window frame shifts the window down, splitting a bottom frame first when there is nothing below. A lone-window frame in a multi-frame tag deliberately does NOTHING (the neither-branch).

content.heading: split-down
content: [$ModShift-b] With >1 window in the focused frame, split a bottom frame and shift the window down into it.

content.heading: shift-left
content: [$ModCtrl-a] Shift the window left; with nothing to the left focus the frame left, else split left and shift the window into the new frame.

content.heading: shift-right
content: [$ModCtrl-e] Shift the window right, else split right and focus the new frame right.

content.heading: new-frame
content: [$ModShift-t] The FRAME LOGIC ONLY of the open-a-second-frame binding: split auto + cycle_frame ONLY when the focused frame holds >0 windows; an empty frame stays as is (the terminal then opens into it). The spawn $TERMINAL half stays a dots concern - herbctl never spawns terminals; the dots keybind chains this with the spawn.

content.heading: split-right-cycle
content: [$Mod-v] Split right at half and cycle into the new frame.

content.heading: split-right-focus
content: [$ModCtrl-v] Split right at half and focus -e right into the new frame (exploding focus).

content.heading: split-bottom-focus
content: [$ModCtrl-b] Split bottom at half and focus -i down into the new frame (insertion focus).

content.heading: close-window
content: [$Mod-q] A focused float is ONLY un-floated; tiling windows get closed, with a lone-window frame removed afterwards (close_and_remove / close_or_remove). Under lock.

content.heading: close-or-remove
content: [$ModShift-q] A focused float is closed and its frame removed; otherwise close_or_remove (close, and remove the frame when it is left empty).

content.heading: xkill-or-close
content: [$ModCtrl-q] The xkill-or-close chain: a focused client exists -> spawn xkill (targeted kill), else close_and_remove.

content.heading: fullscreen-toggle
content: [$ModShift-f] Fullscreen toggle on the focused client.

content.heading: minimize-toggle
content: [$ModShift-z] Minimized toggle on the focused client.

content.heading: The float-register state machines
content: Three bindings carry whole register machines, ported branch for branch:

content.heading: float-focus
content: [$Mod-f] The float-register machine: try focusing a float (un-float it into an EMPTY focused frame; with children the float stays, no stacking) / no floats + max layout -> the size-keeping lift (hc_center frame, vacated-frame removal, hc_fit_to frame, then the algorithm=max tail) / a focused float -> direct un-float (no hc_tile). No script-level lock.

content.heading: float-yank
content: [$Mod-x] The layer-yank machine (the hc_floatx port): focus-a-float-then-unfloat / yank (float + center into the float session, frame left alone) / defer / un-float-into-empty-frame / tidying (remove, reveal, polyframes hidden, use_previous).

content.heading: zoom
content: [$ModCtrl-f] The three-state press machine (the hc_zoom port): tiled -> float (flag reset + center + deco-flush frame fill + fit) / floating -> maximize onto a <tag>-max tag (PF_MAX state owned by the delegated hc_maximize / hc_unmaximize helpers) / maximized -> restore. The -max check runs BEFORE the floating check. Exit 1 when no window is focused.

content.heading: The herbstutil dependency
content: herbctl imports herbstutil for its PURE primitives only - parseAttr, the typed attribute reader. herbctl does not (and must not) import herbstutil's command functions: the composite keybind commands live here, and herbstutil ships none of them.

content.heading: Fail-soft, and pinned by tests
content: Every spawn (herbstclient and the dots helper binaries) carries the 5-second timeout inherited from herbstutil's spawn layer: a vanished window resolves null instead of wedging the bar or the keybind.
Every command is verified against the recorded argv of a mocked herbstclient binary (plus mocked helper binaries) - bun test covers all 25 commands; nothing here needs a live WM to test.
The dots keybinds spawn the compiled standalone binary at ~/.local/bin/herbctl (built with bunli); the dots deployment toolchain (on-deploy) ensures the binary is built and installed.
